question: In context, Lise's reply "Neither does the bank" (paragraph 6) most strongly suggests that she believes the inventory figures:

options.A: matter more to Bram's own planning than to the bank that asked for them.
options.B: need to be close to the truth rather than exact to the last item.
options.C: would be more accurate if every item in the store were counted by hand.
options.D: are checked by the bank only when a drawer looks badly miscounted.

question: According to Passage A, when the author's team fastened mats of moss to the trunks of young shedding trees, most of the mats:

options.A: spread within two seasons to neighboring trees that keep their bark.
options.B: held water against the bark and slowed the growth of the trunks.
options.C: fell away within two seasons on the plates of bark beneath them.
options.D: stayed attached until the trunks began to split into deep furrows.

question: According to the passage, many sketchbooks were taken apart after their owners' deaths so that:

options.A: their best pages could be sold one at a time.
options.B: the notes and arithmetic in them could be thrown out.
options.C: students could study the thumbnails behind paintings.
options.D: museums could display their most finished spreads.

question: The main purpose of the passage is to:

options.A: show that distractions such as mirrors and music reliably make long waits feel much shorter.
options.B: describe how a single winding line serves customers more quickly than several parallel lines.
options.C: explain why faster equipment rarely reduces the complaints that people make about slow service.
options.D: argue that research on waiting points toward honesty with people rather than disguising their waits.
